title: Facility-Initiated Discharge from a Private Pay Long-Term Care Residency
content:
**Administrator's regulatory summary — Private Pay Long-Term Care Residency.**

**Permitted reasons.** The center may discharge a resident only for a reason the federal rules allow: nonpayment, needs the center cannot meet, health improved so the resident no longer needs the services, the safety or health of individuals endangered, or the center closing.

**Notice period.** A facility-initiated discharge notice states a discharge date at least the discharge notice days after the notice date, unless the notice reason is one of the discharge notice exception reasons, in which case notice is given as soon as practicable; a resident who has lived in the center fewer than the short residence days may also be given notice as soon as practicable. This is judged on the agreement's record: the notice date, the planned discharge date, the notice reason and the admission date.

**Nonpayment.** A notice for nonpayment issues only when the oldest unpaid room-and-board charge is at least the nonpayment minimum days past due and no Medicaid application of the resident is pending. Days past due are the calendar days from the due date of the oldest room-and-board charge with an open balance to the handling date. A resident whose Medicaid application has been submitted is not in nonpayment status, and a notice already issued for nonpayment is rescinded when the application is submitted or the past-due balance is paid. The Medicaid application is read from the resident's Medical Assistance Nursing Facility Coverage case.

**Ombudsman copy.** Every notice is copied to the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman.

**Appeal.** The resident is not discharged under the notice while a timely appeal is pending, unless the notice reason is that the safety or the health of individuals is endangered; an appeal decided for the resident rescinds the notice. The appeal is read from the appeal filing date on the agreement.

**Boundary cases (hypothetical, with the 30-day notice period of the tier schedule).**
- Notice delivered on day 1 of a period, nonpayment reason, discharge date stated as day 31: 30 days after the notice date — the period is met.
- The same notice stating day 30: 29 days after — the period is not met.
- A notice for urgent medical needs may state a discharge date as soon as practicable.
- An appeal filed in time against a nonpayment notice: no discharge while it is pending. An appeal against a notice for endangered safety: the discharge is not held back by the appeal.

**Effects.** When the resident leaves under the notice, room and board billed for days after the discharge is credited as a discharge proration; when the notice is rescinded, the planned discharge date is cleared and the stay continues.
